title: Johnny Harmon, Horace Diaz and Vic Pellegrini
summary: More piano players, including Horace Diaz and Vic Pellegrini, and Diaz at the Silver Slipper.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did you work with Johnny Harmon in those days?

I can't remember too well if I worked any jobs with Johnny in those days. I knew of Johnny and had met him and certainly talked with him many times. I can't recall playing any early jobs with Johnny until our association in 1946 at WSMB radio station.
The Lesley Hems records, they sound like nickels, you know. He made two tunes, I forget the date, but the late 20s, Johnny Harmon's Bayou's
was that when he used this piano player, Horace Dias? Was Horace Dias on some of those records with him?

That is a fine piano player that we left out. Horace Dias, I remember him when I was coming up. Another piano player by the name of, see his name's come to you as you go along, a fellow by the name of Pellegrini, Vic Pellegrini. He was a very fine piano player.
Did he play solo or was he playing solo?

Vic played around with bands, and in fact I think he played with Johnny Detroit if I'm not mistaken. And he used to do a lot of early radio work, solo work. Vic Pellegrini was a very, very fine jazz piano player. I would definitely tell him as a jazz piano player.
Horace Dias was a very fine musician and a good piano player and a very good arranger. In fact, I think he's still doing a lot of arranging work for some very fine bands right now.
What happened to him? He's gone.

Oh, well he's up north. I think I asked somebody about him and they said that they had met him and that he was still doing arranging. I think he used to do arranging for Eddie Guchin at one time if I'm not mistaken.
He does a lot of stocks too. Yeah. He played a few of them. Yeah. A lot of all that kind of stuff.

Well, Horace Dias played at the old Silver Slipper when Jink Morton played down there. Which band was this? I was trying to think of the band. Now, I think my brother-in-law Steve Lloyd Cantor had the band. And I know he definitely had him. Steve was on banjo and Horace Dias was on piano. Jink Morton on bass. I can't remember who the clarinet player was and who the trumpet player he had with at that time. But that was a good band of those days too. It was a real good swinging band.
